description: Discovering, modelling, analysing and improving how organisations actually work: processes, activities and roles, BPMN notation, as-is and to-be analysis, process simulation and bottleneck analysis, improvement methods such as Lean and Six Sigma, and workflow automation. Students draw executable BPMN models in the browser, simulate them with queues and resources to find bottlenecks, and redesign a mobile money agent network end to end.
modelledOn: Dumas, La Rosa, Mendling and Reijers, Fundamentals of Business Process Management
Object Management Group, Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) 2.0
Weske, Business Process Management: Concepts, Languages, Architectures
van der Aalst, Process Mining: Data Science in Action
outcomes: Identify an organisation's processes, their activities, roles, inputs and outputs, and organise them into a process architecture.
Model processes correctly in BPMN, including events, gateways, pools, lanes, messages and sub-processes.
Analyse as-is processes qualitatively and quantitatively, finding waste, root causes, cycle times and costs.
Simulate processes with resources and arrival rates to locate bottlenecks and test redesigns before implementation.
Apply improvement methods to design to-be processes and justify them with measured gains.
Automate a process with a workflow engine and monitor its performance with process mining.

units.title: Processes, activities and roles
topics: What a business process is: events, activities, decisions, actors, resources, inputs and outputs
Process orientation versus functional silos; the BPM lifecycle from identification to monitoring
Roles, responsibilities and the RACI matrix
Core, support and management processes; customers and value

units.title: Process identification and discovery
topics: Process architecture: value chains, process landscapes and levels of decomposition
Selecting processes for improvement by importance, health and feasibility
Discovery methods: interviews, workshops, observation, document analysis and event logs
Modelling quality: syntactic, semantic and pragmatic quality; the seven process modelling guidelines

units.title: BPMN notation
topics: Flow objects: tasks, events and gateways; sequence flow
Gateways: exclusive, parallel, inclusive and event-based; splits, joins and correct pairing
Pools, lanes, message flow and collaboration diagrams between organisations
Data objects, data stores and artefacts
Sub-processes, call activities, loops and multi-instance activities
Modelling a cocoa purchasing process from farm gate to licensed buying company

units.title: Advanced BPMN and process correctness
topics: Intermediate events: timers, messages, signals, errors, escalation and compensation; boundary events
Event sub-processes and exception handling
Token semantics; soundness, deadlocks and livelocks; Petri nets in brief
Decision modelling with DMN decision tables alongside BPMN

units.title: As-is and to-be analysis
topics: Value-added, business value-added and non-value-adding activities
Waste analysis with the seven wastes; issue registers and Pareto analysis
Root cause analysis: cause-and-effect diagrams and why-why analysis
Quantitative analysis: cycle time, waiting time, cycle time efficiency and activity-based costing
Flow analysis of sequential, parallel and rework structures; Little's law

units.title: Process simulation and bottlenecks
topics: Queueing fundamentals: arrival rates, service times, utilisation and the M/M/1 and M/M/c models
Discrete-event simulation of BPMN models: arrival distributions, task durations, resource pools and calendars
Identifying bottlenecks from utilisation and waiting times; the theory of constraints
Running scenarios and comparing designs; warm-up, replications and confidence intervals
Simulating queues at a district hospital outpatient department

units.title: Process improvement methods
topics: Redesign heuristics: task elimination, resequencing, parallelism, specialisation and triage
Lean: value stream mapping, flow, pull and continuous improvement
Six Sigma and DMAIC; variation, control charts and process capability
Business process re-engineering and its lessons
Measuring improvement: the devil's quadrangle of time, cost, quality and flexibility
Redesigning loan approval for a rural bank serving susu groups

units.title: Workflow automation
topics: Process-aware information systems and business process management systems
Making a model executable: data, forms, service tasks, user tasks and business rules
Process engines and an open-source BPMN engine such as Camunda or Flowable
Robotic process automation versus workflow orchestration; integration with APIs and SMS
Process mining: event logs, process discovery, conformance checking and performance analysis
Change management and user adoption of automated processes

units.title: Case study: a mobile money agent network
topics: Modelling cash-in, cash-out, registration and float rebalancing across agents and the operator
KYC checks, transaction limits and reversal handling as process rules
Simulating agent queues and float shortages on market days
Proposing and simulating a to-be design with measured gains
Capstone: presenting the as-is model, analysis, simulation and to-be process to stakeholders

schedule.title: Processes, roles and the BPM lifecycle
schedule.exercise: Pick a process you know, such as registering for a national ID or buying at a market stall, and list its events, activities, decisions, actors and outputs in a table.

tasks.title: Draw a first flow diagram of a cash deposit at a bank branch, labelling the start event, five activities, one decision and the end event
Build a RACI matrix for an eight-step student admission process and check that every activity has exactly one accountable role
Classify the processes of a small hospital as core, support or management, and justify your choice for each against a scoring rubric in a case scenario

schedule.title: Process architecture, discovery and modelling quality
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page plan describing how you would discover the real order-fulfilment process of a shop using two discovery methods and their trade-offs.

tasks.title: Draw a three-level process landscape for a cocoa buying company, decomposing each level 1 process into level 2 processes
Rank five candidate processes for improvement by importance, health and feasibility using given evidence, and defend the top choice in the scenario debrief
Review a deliberately messy model of a loan request against the seven process modelling guidelines and produce a corrected version with a list of fixes

schedule.title: BPMN flow objects, gateways and pools
schedule.exercise: Take a short written description of a customer order and mark in the text which words become tasks, events and gateways before drawing it.

tasks.title: Model a simple library book request using start and end events, four tasks and sequence flow, with no dangling flows
Model an order that is checked in parallel for stock and payment, with an exclusive gateway for fraud and correctly paired split and join gateways
Build a collaboration diagram between a customer, a shop and a courier with pools, lanes and message flows, and trace one order end to end

schedule.title: Data, sub-processes and the cocoa purchasing process
schedule.exercise: Write a short note on when to use a sub-process, a call activity and a loop, with one example of each from a purchasing process.

tasks.title: Add data objects and a data store for farmer records to an existing purchasing model and mark each task that reads or writes them
Model weighing of multiple bags per farmer with a multi-instance sub-process and a reusable call activity for quality grading
Model the full cocoa purchase from farm gate to licensed buying company across farmer, buying agent and company pools, covering rejection, payment and haulage

schedule.title: Events, exceptions and process correctness
schedule.exercise: Take a BPMN model with a suspected deadlock, trace the tokens by hand and write what is wrong and how to fix it.

tasks.title: Add a timer boundary event to an approval task so an escalation occurs after 48 hours, and describe the token path for both outcomes
Trace tokens through a given model, find the deadlock caused by a mismatched gateway pair, and redraw it so it is sound
Write a DMN decision table for loan eligibility using age, income and group savings history, and test it on eight applicant cases in the scenario

schedule.title: As-is analysis, waste and flow measures
schedule.exercise: Calculate cycle time efficiency for a three-step process with given processing and waiting times and write two sentences interpreting the result.

tasks.title: Mark every activity of a given 10-step claims process as value-adding, business value-adding or non-value-adding and count each type
Compute cycle time, waiting time and cycle time efficiency for a process with sequential and parallel branches from given figures, and check your sums against the tool
Analyse a rework loop in a passport-style application process using Little's law and cost per case, then recommend one change in the scenario and score the effect

schedule.title: Queueing and discrete-event simulation
schedule.exercise: Explain in a paragraph why a server with 90 percent utilisation produces long queues even though it is not overloaded.

tasks.title: Plot the average queue length of an M/M/1 queue for utilisation from 0.1 to 0.95 and mark where waiting becomes unacceptable
Attach arrival rates, task durations and a pool of three clerks to a service model and run the simulation to read waiting times and utilisation
Find the bottleneck in a simulated five-step process with given resource calendars, then test whether adding one resource moves the bottleneck elsewhere

schedule.title: Scenario comparison and the outpatient department
schedule.exercise: Write a short report recommending one of two redesigned queue layouts, citing mean waiting time and a confidence interval for each.

tasks.title: Run a model with 10 replications and a warm-up period, then report the mean waiting time and a 95 percent confidence interval
Compare two staffing scenarios by computing the difference in mean waiting time and checking whether the confidence intervals overlap
Redesign the flow of a district hospital outpatient department with triage and extra consulting rooms, simulate three options and select one within a budget limit

schedule.title: Redesign heuristics, Lean and Six Sigma
schedule.exercise: Pick a slow process from daily life and apply three redesign heuristics to it, noting for each what is gained and what could go wrong.

tasks.title: Apply task elimination and resequencing to a given order process diagram, and redraw the model showing which tasks were removed or moved
Draw a value stream map for a bakery order from raw flour to delivered bread, including process time, lead time and inventory between steps
Plot a control chart from 30 measurements of delivery time, flag out-of-control points and compute process capability against a target

schedule.title: Re-engineering and the rural bank loan redesign
schedule.exercise: Write a half-page lesson learned from a failed re-engineering project and say how you would avoid the same mistake in a rural bank.

tasks.title: Decide in a re-engineering case which process changes to push through and which to pilot, and score your choices against the lessons rubric
Compute time, cost, quality and flexibility scores for an as-is and a to-be design, and plot both on a devil's quadrangle chart
Redesign loan approval for a rural bank serving susu groups, producing as-is and to-be models, and justify each change with a measured gain

schedule.title: Workflow automation and executable models
schedule.exercise: List which tasks in a given process should be user tasks, service tasks or business rule tasks, giving a reason for each choice.

tasks.title: Mark each element of a leave request model with the information system role that supports it and note what the system stores or decides
Make a loan approval model executable by adding forms, a service task for credit check and a business rule task, listing the data each needs
Choose and configure a process engine for a small business in a scenario, balancing cost, skills and support, and justify the choice to the owner

schedule.title: Automation choices, process mining and adoption
schedule.exercise: Draft a short staff communication explaining what an automated approval process changes for clerks, and how you will support them during the switch.

tasks.title: Choose between robotic process automation and workflow orchestration for four given tasks and record the reasons in the scenario rubric
Discover the process model from a small event log of 20 cases by counting directly-follows pairs, and list the variants found
Plan the rollout of an automated process, choosing training, pilot sites and feedback steps under a limited budget, and handle resistance from two staff groups

schedule.title: Mobile money agent network case study
schedule.exercise: Prepare a ten-minute stakeholder presentation outline that moves from the as-is model to the measured to-be design for the agent network.

tasks.title: Model cash-in and cash-out between a customer, an agent and the operator, showing where float moves at each step
Add KYC checks, transaction limits and a reversal path to the cash-out model as gateways and sub-processes, and test with five sample transactions
Simulate the as-is and a to-be agent model for a market day with float rebalancing, and report waiting time, shortages and cost for both
